articles.title: Pete Golding Addresses Report Ole Miss Hired FBI to Search Lane Kiffin's Office After Exit to LSU
articles.summary: Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding told reporters Monday "there was no hiring process with the FBI" after Walker Jones, who is the executive director of the school's NIL collective, said the FBI searched the Rebels' football office after Lane Kiffin left for LSU.
articles.body:
Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding told reporters Monday "there was no hiring process with the FBI" after Walker Jones, who is the executive director of the school's NIL collective, said the FBI searched the Rebels' football office after Lane Kiffin left for LSU.

"Any playoff game, you're gonna up security," Golding said, per ESPN's Mark Schlabach . "There was no hiring process with the FBI. I think we probably have a current player whose father happens to work for the FBI and lives in town. ... You want to make sure it's secure for your players—the video access and everything. All those things you're doing regardless of where you're at."

Schlabach noted Jones told the Assorted Crackers podcast the FBI conducted a search for bugs in the football office following Kiffin's departure.

The comments are just the latest chapter in the saga that is Kiffin's departure.

There was no shortage of speculation about whether he would leave for LSU or Florida all while guiding the Rebels to a College Football Playoff spot last season. He eventually chose the Tigers, which led to drama regarding which coaches would leave with him and which would stay with Ole Miss.

ESPN's Schlabach and Pete Thamel reported at the time that athletic director Keith Carter and chancellor Glenn Boyce "were adamant" Kiffin could not coach in the CFP.

"Ole Miss doesn't want Kiffin around its players with the transfer portal opening on Jan. 2," they reported. "The Rebels also don't want their CFP games to be a 'commercial' for LSU's future under Kiffin."

Ole Miss offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr., co-offensive coordinator/tight ends coach Joe Cox, receivers coach George McDonald, running backs coach Kevin Smith and general manager Billy Glasscock ended up joining Kiffin at LSU, although Weis, McDonald and Cox were among those who stayed for the CFP.

The Rebels ended up advancing to the semifinals with wins over Tulane and Georgia before they fell to Miami by just four points.

Ultimately, just four Ole Miss players transferred to LSU to join Kiffin and the other coaches with defensive end Princewill Umanmielen, linebacker TJ Dottery, receiver Winston Watkins Jr. and offensive tackle Devin Harper choosing the Tigers.

Star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy were among those who stayed with the Rebels.

The two SEC rivals face each other at Ole Miss on Sept. 19 in what is surely going to be seen as one of the games of the season.

articles.title: Luís Castro: "El resultado es justo, pero si hubiera ganado un equipo, hubiéramos sido nosotros"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador luso ha confirmado la salida de Kareem Tunde y ha matizado que, la ausencia de Musuayi, se debe a una sanción del pasado
articles.summary: El entrenador luso ha confirmado la salida de Kareem Tunde y ha matizado que, la ausencia de Musuayi, se debe a una sanción del pasado
articles.body: Luís Castro se ha marchado con mejores sensaciones con la que se marchó del RCDE Stadium la semana pasada. El técnico luso ha calificado que la imagen del equipo "es otra cosa. Hemos tenido las oportunidades más claras y hemos tenido identidad". Así mismo, el portugués ha confirmado la salida de Kareem Tunde y ha dejado abierta la posibilidad de otras ventas de la plantilla y la factible incorporación de alguna cara nueva, "siempre y cuando mejoren al equipo".  Un Levante competitivo, diferente al del Espanyol: "Es otra cosa. Jugamos fuera, en un campo muy difícil, y has peleado para intentar ganar. Las oportunidades más claras han sido nuestras y hemos tenido identidad. Mejorando un poco las situaciones tácticas y los jugadores que han venido, cuando estén más tiempo, mejorará todo" Jugadores inscritos sin minutos: "Thiago ha jugado titular y no estaba inscrito. El equipo estaba bien y los cambios los hemos hecho para refrescar. Estábamos en el campo adversario y ellos estaban haciendo balones largos. Estábamos entrenado en el área y con más situaciones ofensivas que ellos. Por eso no hemos hecho cambios. El equipo estaba bien, pero los que han llegado necesitan tiempo para estar con nosotros" Kareem Tunde: "Yo pienso que saldrá. No sé si está confirmado, pero saldrá. No estoy muy preocupado de eso" Empate justo: "El resultado es justo y pienso que, si hubiera ganado un equipo, lo hubiéramos ganado nosotros. Pero el resultado es justo. Ellos también han tenido algunas situaciones, pero pienso que las más claras la hemos tenido nosotros" Musuayi, sanción del pasado: "No ha jugado por una expulsión, pero no lo comprendo. Él ha tenido una expulsión y después de haber estado suspendido, pero ha jugado en Bélgica. Yo no comprendo eso. Después de la suspensión, ha jugado, y ahora no puedo. Yo no comprendo eso. Si juegas en competición y ahora está sancionado, yo no comprendo esto. Yo lo quería tener en el banquillo porque es un jugador que ha trabajado muy bien" Actuación de Osasuna: "Es un equipo que tiene calidad. Individualmente son muy fuertes y los delanteros tienen mucha calidad. Colectivamente crecerá. En algunos momentos del partido nos han hecho daño y creo que es un equipo que tendrá un campeonato normal" Necesidades futbolísticas ante la marcha de Kareem: "En primer lugar, tenemos el fair play financiero que no ayuda. El club está dando la vida para encontrar soluciones. Si tenemos oportunidades, hasta que no termine el mercado estamos abiertos, pero fichar jugadores por fichar, no queremos. Dependemos de la liga y el fair play. Estamos contentos por Kareem que ha trabajado muy bien y lo merece" Posible venta de Carlos Álvarez: "Todos pueden salir. Carlos no ha tenido minutos porque yo lo he decidido. Necesitábamos otras cosas para el partido de hoy, pero todos los jugadores del Levante y yo también, estamos preparados para salir. Yo es una situación de uno u otro. El mercado está abierto. Si hay ofertas buenas, puede salir uno u otro"

articles.title: Qué pasa si quedan empate en Cuartos de Final de Leagues Cup 2026: ¿Hay tiempo extra o penales?
articles.standfirst: Descubre cuál es el criterio de desempate para los partidos de América, Monterrey, León, Toluca en la Leagues Cup
articles.summary: Descubre cuál es el criterio de desempate para los partidos de América, Monterrey, León, Toluca en la Leagues Cup
articles.body: La emoción de los Cuartos de Final de la Leagues Cup 2026 llegará esta semana con cuatro clubes de la Liga MX todavía en competencia. Pero cuando un partido de eliminación directa termina igualado después de los 90 minutos, surge una pregunta clave: ¿se juega tiempo extra o todo se define desde el punto penal? La respuesta es directa: no habrá tiempos extra. Si Monterrey, León, Toluca o América terminan empatados con sus respectivos rivales de la MLS al finalizar el tiempo reglamentario, el boleto a las Semifinales se decidirá inmediatamente mediante una tanda de penales. A diferencia de otros torneos, la Leagues Cup 2026 no contempla tiempos extra en sus rondas de eliminación directa. Si los 90 minutos terminan con igualdad, los jugadores deberán acudir directamente al manchón penal. Esto significa que no importa si el marcador queda 0-0, 1-1 o cualquier otro empate: el ganador de la tanda avanzará a las Semifinales. El formato busca evitar que los encuentros se prolonguen y mantener un calendario más dinámico para los equipos de la Liga MX y la MLS. En la primera fase del torneo, el sistema de puntos es diferente, pues un empate también se resuelve mediante penales: Sin embargo, en los Cuartos de Final de la Leagues Cup ya no hay puntos en disputa: el ganador de los penales obtiene el boleto a la siguiente ronda. Los Cuartos de Final se jugarán entre el martes 25 y el miércoles 26 de agosto de 2026, con cuatro enfrentamientos que definirán a los semifinalistas. Estos son los partidos programados: Los horarios corresponden al tiempo del centro de México. Monterrey, León, Toluca y América buscarán mantener con vida a la Liga MX frente a los representantes de la MLS. Así que los aficionados deben estar preparados para una definición desde los once pasos. Si hay empate después de 90 minutos, no habrá prórroga: habrá penales. Con cuatro cruces por delante, cualquier error desde el punto penal podría definir quién continúa soñando con el título de la Leagues Cup 2026.

articles.title: Liverpool: Florian Wirtz part of potentially a worst-ever transfer window, says Jamie Carragher as Reds' midfield problems exposed
articles.summary: Liverpool drew their opening Premier League fixture 2-2 at Newcastle on Sunday but Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher explained on Monday Night Football why the Reds' midfield set-up - and lack of impact from Florian Wirtz - is a big problem for new boss Andoni Iraola.
articles.body:
During a damning assessment of the Reds' midfield set-up in their 2-2 draw at Newcastle, Carragher also explained the big weakness in new boss Andoni Iraola's tactical approach at Liverpool and why it will prevent them from launching a Premier League title challenge this season.

Here's how the Sky Sports pundit broke down Liverpool's big issues on Monday Night Football...

"I don't believe that midfield can function with the personnel in there," said Carragher. "For me, it doesn't work. And it's not just about personnel, it's the structure the manager is asking."

Liverpool fielded Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai in midfield at St James' Park, with Florian Wirtz at No 10.

However, rather than sitting in a double pivot, Szoboszlai often moved forward into more attacking areas.

Carragher noted how Man City have had success in the past with a double-pivot and No 10 set-up but added: "Why did [Pep] Guardiola always bring his full-backs inside? Because the holding midfield player needed help to stop counter-attacks. Straight away that's a problem for me [with Liverpool].

Carragher showed examples of not only Szoboszlai but also Gravenberch charging forwards to join Wirtz and emptying the midfield - providing space for Newcastle to counter-attack into.

"All they think about is going forwards. All three of them. And that's why it can't work," said Carragher.

"I don't think I've ever seen a more offensive team, or players who think offensively in the Premier League than that. There's only the two centre-backs who don't think about going forward."

Carragher also noted how it appears to be an instruction from Iraola for Wirtz and Szoboszlai to 'lock on' to opposition midfielders.

However, while Brentford had success employing a similarly aggressive tactic against Tottenham because their centre-backs stepped up to close the space behind, Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk didn't make the same move. Instead, the 35-year-old centre-back sat deeper.

"You've got a situation, like at Man Utd under Erik ten Hag a few years ago - a team who want to press high but with a deep block.

"That's why these big holes are appearing. The midfield players want to lock on and Van Dijk does not want to come with them."

On Van Dijk, Carragher added: "He needs protecting, he needs cuddling, he needs looking after."

After watching Liverpool against Newcastle, Carragher says it is now essential they sign a holding midfielder to offer them more security against fast breaks.

"Liverpool need someone alongside Gravenberch," said Carragher. "It doesn't necessarily need to be a player who can't get on the ball and he's just tackling and stopping players. If you play for one of the top teams in the world, you need to be able to get hold of the ball. But I want someone who can run.

If a holding midfielder comes in alongside Gravenberch and Szoboszlai goes to No 10, where does Wirtz go?

Carragher doesn't see a suitable role for him in the Liverpool team with Iraola's set-up.

He says the German's lack of end product with Liverpool - just five goals and three assists in 33 Premier League appearances last season - means it is fair to question whether he will ever be the answer.

"This thing that it takes people a year to settle in the Premier League, I think is a bit of a myth. I don't think there's too many examples where it does," said Carragher.

"I've always seen this coming. When people are saying [Wirtz] has got to go to No 10, that means Szoboszlai's got to be in the team and he's not a central midfield player.

"I thought this would come up in six weeks, I think it's coming up right now. I don't see where he fits in at all, really.

"What's Iraola going to do with Wirtz? You can't keep going with it, it's not working

"It didn't work last season. Liverpool last season conceded 78 goals, 53 in the Premier League, the most they've ever conceded in the Premier League. And all of a sudden it's all about buying wingers?

"I'm not sure where he fits. I almost thought you could put him in a pocket from the left, where he plays for Germany, but Iraola loves wingers, he wants players who've got energy up and down the flank.

"I don't think we're seeing a massive underperformance. I think what we've seen for a year is probably what he is, which is a neat and tidy footballer. Not a player who should be worth £110m, someone who probably should be £50m-60m, something like that. Neat and tidy, lovely touch. I'm not sure what people are expecting."

Worst transfer window in Premier League history?

Wirtz was part of an enormous £445m transfer spend by Liverpool last summer, when it appeared they were out to supercharge Arne Slot's Premier League title-winning squad. Instead it went badly wrong, with Liverpool limping home in fifth, with Slot sacked.

As well as Wirtz, Liverpool also signed Alexander Isak for a Premier League record £125m, Hugo Ekitike (£79m), Milos Kerkez (£40m), Jeremie Frimpong (£29.5m), Giorgi Mamardashvili (£29m) and Giovanni Leoni (£26m).

Carragher reckons that transfer window may have hurt Liverpool more than it helped them. In fact, he reckons it could go down as the worst summer of business by a Premier League club ever.

"My fear is this window of 12 months ago could set Liverpool back a year or two to fix it," he said.

"Don't forget, last season it was not about these players. Because it was all about Arne Slot and his style of playing, and he's not like Jurgen Klopp, and he's holding his players back...

"But we're talking 12 months of under-performance from all of these players except Ekitike.

"If this doesn't change in the next two or three months, under Iraola, and these players improve, I think we're going to be looking at that as arguably the worst transfer window we've probably seen in Premier League history.

"When you consider the fees for these players, and what it was going to do for Liverpool... The idea wasn't for these players coming in just to be good players, it was to create something like a little dynasty for Liverpool.

"Let's not forget, Liverpool won the league two years ago. These were supposed to do what City have done in the last few years, or Manchester United in the past, where they've gone and won two or three leagues in five years."

With all that in mind, Carragher has little hope of his former club mounting a serious title challenge this season.

"I don't think Liverpool will be contenders this season," he said. "Liverpool are in transition

"I'm not trying to make excuses for them, because they've lost [Mohamed] Salah, Van Dijk is probably going to go, maybe this is his last season, and the goalkeeper Alisson. You're talking about three all-time greats there for Liverpool.

"So they're probably not going to be there in 12 months and these [signings of summer 2025] have got to find their feet, and Iraola has got to find his feet at a big club.

"For me, if Liverpool qualify for the Champions League this season, I'd be happy. The manager sort of beds in and then you can maybe go from there and look to challenge."

articles.title: Lane Kiffin Denies Calling Browns' Todd Monken While Recruiting Dae'Quan Wright to LSU
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken claimed that Lane Kiffin called him to ask about Dae'Quan Wright, but the LSU head coach denied that claim on Monday.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken claimed that Lane Kiffin called him to ask about Dae'Quan Wright, but the LSU head coach denied that claim on Monday.

"There's some inaccuracies in that story, but I don't know," Kiffin said. "Maybe someone else called him that said they were me. I actually don't know Todd. I guess somebody left him a text or called him that was me, cause I don't know him or have his number."

Wright, 22, went undrafted in the 2026 NFL draft and joined the Philadelphia Eagles before being claimed off waivers by the Browns earlier this month. Cleveland released him on Monday, and his agents say he will join LSU if he clears waivers.

Monken said in his availability last week that as far as he knew, Wright had a medical issue that "wasn't allowing him to practice" and that the decision to release him had "nothing to do with me."

Monken also said Kiffin had called him, but he didn't return the call.

"I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago. Now I know," Monken said. "S--t, I didn't know, now I know. I didn't call him back, guess I should've"

Wright is believed to be the first player to reach an agreement to return to the collegiate level after being signed by an NFL team as an undrafted free agent. The move also would reunite Wright with his former coach.

The tight end spent the first two years of his college career with Virginia Tech before playing for Ole Miss in 2024 and 2025. Last season, he had 635 yards and five touchdowns.

Wright is one of several college football players fighting for another year of eligibility after the NCAA passed new eligibility rules that give athletes a five-year window to play at the college level.

Louisiana's 19th Judicial District Court passed a temporary restraining order last week that would allow more than 30 college athletes and 16 former college football players to play another year. Several of those players, like Wright, are on NFL training camp rosters.

Jack Pyburn, a former LSU linebacker who is currently with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, could also join the Wright, Kiffin and the Tigers this season.

Whether Kiffin is actually recruiting NFL players is another question that could open a new can of worms, but he claims not to have reached out to Monken.

articles.title: Aubameyang, el salvavidas del Dépor
articles.standfirst: Gracias a sus goles le sirven al Depor sumar dos puntos y seguir sin perder
articles.summary: Gracias a sus goles le sirven al Depor sumar dos puntos y seguir sin perder
articles.body: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang es un fichaje de muchos kilates para un Deportivo que vuelve a Primera tras ocho temporadas sin jugar en la máxima categoría. Para el deportivismo es ya un ídolo y un ejemplo para el resto de la plantilla. Tras más de 400 goles en toda su carrera el internacional gabonés lleva dos goles en los dos primeros partidos con la camiseta blanquiazul. Dos goles que suman los dos puntos que tiene el Dépor en su casillero. Desde Bebeto no marcaba un jugador debutante en los dos primeros partidos de Liga. Aubameyang ha llegado a La Coruña para triunfar y para ayudar al equipo a conseguir la salvación. Dentro de la plantilla ya ejerce de capitán y no para de ayudar a los futbolistas más jóvenes. Para el ex del Marsella es muy bonito el cariño que le está mostrando toda la ciudad. “Me han recibido muy bien y estoy encantado con llegar a un equipo que ya lo conocía desde que comencé en Alemania”, comentaba el ‘7’ gallego. En su presentación el delantero fue muy claro. “Vengo a hacer goles, a dar asistencias y sobre todo a ganar muchos partidos”, expresaba hace unos días.

articles.title: Reencuentro con abrazo cariñoso entre Arbeloa y Xabi Alonso
articles.standfirst: Vuelven a verse tras el cambio de papeles en el Real Madrid la pasada temporada
articles.summary: Vuelven a verse tras el cambio de papeles en el Real Madrid la pasada temporada
articles.body: El Fulham-Chelsea dejó una imagen esperadísima: la del reencuentro de Xabi Alonso y Álvaro Arbeloa. Dos entrenadores españoles que compartieron vestuario durante muchos años en varios equipos y que el año pasado protagonizaron un relevo sonado en el banquillo del Real Madrid, cuando el club blanco despidió al ahora entrenador del Chelsea y ascendió a Arbeloa al primer equipo. Coincidieron en Liverpool, Real Madrid y selección española. Juntos jugaron un total de 262 partidos y conquistaron ligas, Champions, Eurocopa y Mundial. Sin embargo, uno de los clubes que los unió, el Real Madrid, abrió una grieta entre ellos por el apresurado despido de Xabi. A final de temporada, Arbeloa también tuvo que marcharse del Bernabéu y ambos han tenido que buscarse la vida en la Premier, concretamente en clubes de Londres. La cercanía ha provocado que su relación vuelva a ser cercana, puesto que sus familias se conocen bien y la cordialidad entre ambos nunca desapareció. El abrazo y las muestras de cariño mutuas en la banda durante el encuentro deja claro que la relación entre dos de los técnicos españoles que este año compiten en la Premier es amistosa.

articles.title: New CFB Rumors on Deion Sanders, Belichick, Lincoln Riley & Norvell Hot Seats, Contract Buyouts
articles.summary: Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports compiled his annual "coaching hot seat list" for college football on Monday, polling people in the "college administrative, search firm and agent world" with findings based on the "expertise and knowledge from industry insiders, some of whom are already positioning themselves for a search or expecting one at a particular school."
articles.body:
Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports compiled his annual "coaching hot seat list" for college football on Monday, polling people in the "college administrative, search firm and agent world" with findings based on the "expertise and knowledge from industry insiders, some of whom are already positioning themselves for a search or expecting one at a particular school."

Among the most notable names on the hot seat were Florida State's Mike Norvell, North Carolina's Bill Belichick and Wisconsin's Luke Fickell, while Oklahoma's Lincoln Riley and Colorado's Deion Sanders are on the warm seat.

On Norvell, Dellenger noted that "school administrators thought long and hard about dismissing Norvell last season," and the surprise may be that Florida State stuck with him for another season. In six years, Norvell's Seminoles have managed just two winning seasons and are 7-17 in the past two campaigns.

It's likely that Norvell was saved by the $50 million buyout in his contract, but he can't afford another disappointing campaign.

Belichick went 4-8 in his first season at North Carolina and his relationship with Jordon Hudson was a persistent storyline and distraction. His general manager, Michael Lombardi, has been placed on administrative leave by the school. Defensive coordinator Steve Belichick is currently on medical leave. And questions about whether Belichick could adjust from the NFL game to college very much remain unanswered.

At Wisconsin, Fickell has gone just 17-21, though Dellenger noted that "the university didn't jump into NIL with both feet" and "administrators have acknowledged that fact and last year made the decision to invest in the roster instead of paying Fickell's whopping buyout."

But the athletic director who hired him, Chris McIntosh, is no longer in Madison. Anything less than a winning season probably doesn't cut it for Fickell.

USC's Riley has a buyout figure around $60 million, though the Trojans have failed to reach double-digit wins in the past three seasons and patience is wearing thin.

As Dellenger wrote, "There are no more excuses. He's been given the resources and has a new general manager and defensive coordinator (Gary Patterson!). Without a playoff trip this year, AD Jen Cohen may finally pull the trigger despite the whopping buyout figure."

Finally, Sanders brought the national spotlight to Colorado and made the Buffs a cultural phenomenon, though the wins haven't followed. The 9-4 campaign in 2024 has been sandwiched by 4-8 and 3-9 seasons, and Sanders has dealt with a number of medical concerns.

As Dellenger reported, "the Buffs need to show marked improvement if Sanders plans to stick around long term."

articles.title: Deion Sanders Says Subpoena in Son Shilo's Bankruptcy Case Not a Distraction Ahead of Season Opener
articles.summary: BOULDER, Colo. (AP) — Deion Sanders has a knack for staying in the headlines whether it's on the field or in court proceedings.
articles.body:
BOULDER, Colo. (AP) — Deion Sanders has a knack for staying in the headlines whether it's on the field or in court proceedings.

The Colorado football coach recently had a sheriff's deputy show up on campus in an attempt to serve him civil papers as part of a bankruptcy trial involving his son, Shilo. Several days later, his lawyer filed a motion to dismiss the case involving some logos the coach uses on boxer briefs, cowboy hats and other things he sells on his website.

The legal wrangling comes with the clock ticking toward Colorado's season opener at Georgia Tech on Sept. 3.

Sanders bristled at the notion any of it was a distraction for a team that has become familiar with them since bringing on a celebrity coach.

"Do you think that's my first subpoena?" Sanders said Monday regarding the Boulder County Sheriff's Office attempt to deliver a subpoena on Aug. 11 in the case involving his son. "When you have 'it,' when you're 'him,' you get sued. You have off-the-field foolishness that if someone really sat down and explained it to you, you would say, 'You've got to be kidding. But it is what it is.

"I don't know anyone that's a game-changer, a way-maker, that is not dealing with some type of lawsuit."

Shilo Sanders' bankruptcy case stems from an incident with a security guard when he was in high school. The guard filed a lawsuit against Sanders and was issued a default judgment when Sanders didn't show for his court date. The original suit said the guard sustained permanent injuries.

"You know Shilo won this is case previously, right? Anybody know that?" Sanders said Monday as he kicks off his fourth season at Colorado on the heels of a 3-9 campaign. "Raise your hand if you knew that. That Shilo got awarded money for this. OK. Check it out.

"I can't wait until it's over and he gets to tell his story. He already won this case."

Deion Sanders faces a separate and unrelated lawsuit in U.S. District Court in Nebraska involving the use of logos. The suit was filed more than a year ago by the man who designed them, Alan Tipp.

Created as part of an Under Armour sunglasses deal, it didn't succeed commercially, according to the court filing by Sanders' attorney last Friday. After Sanders' deal with the apparel company expired, the company allowed him to keep the logos. In the motion to dismiss filed by Sanders' attorney it said the designer "messaged Sanders over the course of several years to express gratitude that the logos were still being used.

"Nevertheless, after lying in wait for close to a decade, on January 30, 2025, Tipp filed this action against Sanders, his merchandising company Prime Time Enterprises, Inc., and his management company, SMAC Entertainment, LLC, claiming he is owed millions of dollars in damages for the supposed unauthorized use of 'his' work."

articles.title: Valencia - Betis | Segunda prueba de nivel de hastío en Mestalla: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: La grada estalló al final del primer partido de Liga ante el Celta (0-0) contra el técnico y los jugadores
articles.summary: La grada estalló al final del primer partido de Liga ante el Celta (0-0) contra el técnico y los jugadores
articles.body: Parece exagerado plantear la segunda jornada de Liga como un ejercicio para templar los nervios de una afición. Pero el final del partido contra el Celta se convirtió en una nueva escalada de reproches de la grada del Valencia contra su entrenador, Carlos Corberán, y también contra los futbolistas. Mestalla esperó al pitido final para recuperar sensaciones y reacciones que recuerdan al hastío que se arrastra desde la temporada pasada. El Betis, además, es un rival Champions que arrancó el curso con victoria. Con el ambiente enrarecido tras el empate frente al Celta, aunque con la convicción por parte del entrenador de que los cinco defensas pueden ser una buena opción para construir una base que no sea solo circunstancial. La baja de Justin de Haas permitirá que Diakhaby entre en el once titular y las dudas vienen por la escasa producción ofensiva que mostró el equipo hace tres días. Si el entrenador insiste en Danjuma, podría acompañarlo de Hugo Duro por probar una combinación diferente que pueda aumentar el número de ocasiones. Los tres puntos logrados el pasado viernes en el estreno liguero ante la Real Sociedad, un rival directo, permiten al Betis llegar a Mestalla repleto de confianza y sumando refuerzos a su expedición: el irlandés Troy Parrott, última incorporación al plantel, viajó con el equipo y podría tener sus primeros minutos como verdiblanco. Pellegrini sigue sin poder contar por diferentes problemas físicos con Diego Conde, Ruibal, Lo Celso, Abde, Morante y Petit, al tiempo que espera un final de mercado que, independientemente de lo que ocurra con Dani Ceballos, un nombre más vinculado a los deseos del club que del propio técnico, le traiga un pivote defensivo con la figura del marroquí Amrabat como prioridad absoluta. Hasta entonces, intentará seguir su buena dinámica en sus visitas a Mestalla, donde suma cuatro triunfos y un empate en sus seis últimas visitas.

articles.summary: La leyenda de las Águilas pidió por uno de los hombres más importantes del club azulcrema
articles.body: Uno de los futbolistas más importantes en la historia del América, Carlos Reinoso, apareció este inicio de semana en su cuenta de X (Antes Twitter) para pedirle a sus seguidores que envairan una oración para un miembro del club que ha pasado prácticamente su vida en el club y está pasando por un momento delicado de salud. El hoy analista de TUDN recordó al Doctor Alfonso Díaz, quien fuera pieza clave en el interior del club, trabajando por más de 40 años, con un trabajo impecable y que en su momento le permitió llegar hasta la Selección Mexicana.  Carlos Reinoso que el fin de semana compartió algunos mensajes en su cuenta de X con respecto al paso del América y también recordó a André Jardine, pero al iniciar la semana publicó que este día sería operado el Doctor Alfonso Díaz, quien tiene más de 50 años trabajando para el cuadro azulcrema. "Buen día para todos. Hoy operan a mi hermano, el doctor Alfonso Díaz, vamos a orar por él amigos americanistas. QDLB". escribrió Carlos Reinoso, quien tiene una gran amistad con el doctor, con quien además compartió momentos desde sus últimos años como jugador y también durante sus diferentes etapas como entrenador. El Doctor Alfonso Díaz llegó al América en 1976, comenzando un vínculo con Carlos Reinoso y además ha visto pasar grandes figuras, encargándose de su recuperación y lesiones, como Luis Roberto Alves 'Zague', Crístobal Ortega, Alfredo Tena, Iván Zamorano y muchos más.  El Doctor Alfonso Díaz recibió un homenaje en el 2021, luego de más de 40 años al servicio del América, de hecho, el consultorio médico que está en las instalaciones de Coapa, lleva su nombre

articles.title: Cole Palmer & Morgan Rogers shine in Chelsea win but Robert Sanchez struggles
articles.summary: While Chelsea's front three produced a sparkling display in their win over Fulham, goalkeeper Robert Sanchez remains a major concern.
articles.body:
If football is won in both boxes, it seems as though Chelsea have one far better covered than the other.

Xabi Alonso began his Stamford Bridge reign with an entertaining 3-2 Premier League win at west London rivals Fulham on Monday - and their new-look front three stole the show.

Morgan Rogers, making his debut after his club record £117m summer move from Aston Villa , combined with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro to produce a devastating attacking display.

All three scored, with Palmer in particular looking back to his best after a difficult year hampered by injuries, culminating in his omission from England's World Cup squad.

At the other end, though, questions remain over goalkeeper Robert Sanchez after two errors contributed to Fulham 's goals from Josh King and Gonzalo Garcia.

Alonso said his front three needed to "lead the rest" so that the "other ones will follow".

But Sanchez has some catching up to do - and when asked about his mistakes, Alonso could only stress the collective responsibility of the team.

"We need to accept and learn from them [the mistakes]," said the Spaniard. "This is going to be a process.

"All the lines, from the strikers, the midfielders, the defence, the goalkeepers, we want to do better in everything."

After the match, ex- Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher - a former team-mate of Alonso - said on Sky Sports that Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro are "as good as anything in the Premier League right now".

He also said they would "never win the league with Sanchez in goal".

It took Joao Pedro just 31 seconds to open the scoring, latching on to a pass from Palmer and lifting his shot over Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno for Chelsea 's fastest goal since October 2016.

After King equalised, Rogers marked his debut with a goal before half-time by tapping in from close range.

But it was Palmer - scorer of Chelsea 's third - who stood out most.

He has endured a frustrating 18 months since a niggling groin problem disrupted his sensational start to life at Stamford Bridge, highlighted by the fact he matched last season's Premier League assist tally by setting up Joao Pedro.

His trickery and creativity was on display throughout against Fulham , along with an impressive work-rate. This was more like the Palmer we saw during his first season at Stamford Bridge - and like the one who tore Paris St-Germain apart during last year's Club World Cup final.

"Over the summer I rested, I recharged and, yeah, I'm ready and I'm hungry," Palmer, who is now just two goals away from 50 in the Premier League, told Sky Sports.

During Chelsea 's pre-season tour of Australia, he spoke of having a point to prove and admitted a lengthy summer break felt unusual after featuring in major tournaments in each of the previous three years.

"Cole Palmer was sensational," said former Manchester United defender Gary Neville on Sky Sports. "Him and Morgan Rogers were electric with Joao Pedro - the front three were brilliant.

"That tonight was the old Cole Palmer. It was unbelievable to watch. One of the best things I've seen this weekend."

How two best mates and Joao Pedro linked up

While Palmer and Joao Pedro have generally carried Chelsea 's biggest attacking threat in recent times, they have now been joined by the impressive Rogers.

His arrival reunites him with Palmer, an ex- Manchester City team-mate and someone he described after the win at Craven Cottage as his "best friend in football".

"He had a difficult season with injuries and stuff last year - and you could see it in his eyes in pre-season and training that he's ready this year and ready to prove people wrong," said Rogers when asked about Palmer's display.

"You saw that with that performance. He was the best player on the pitch by a mile and that's what he does. It's good to have him on our side."

Indeed, it was also encouraging how Rogers, whose pre-season was shortened by his involvement in England's run to third place at the World Cup, looked so fit and powerful.

Rogers is the first Chelsea player to score on his Premier League debut since Christopher Nkunku in 2023 - and the first to create five chances in his first league appearance since records began in 2003-04.

This was also the first time Chelsea supporters sang the new Rogers chant in the away end.

Like Palmer, Joao Pedro missed out on the World Cup - as a high-profile omission from Brazil's squad - but returned in pre-season with eight goals in seven games.

It was no surprise to see him on the scoresheet so early in the Premier League campaign, having inherited the number nine shirt from Liam Delap, who was left out of the squad on Monday, and following the contract extension the Brazilian signed at the weekend.

"Great combination, great quality," Alonso told BBC Match of the Day when asked about his front three.

"We know if we reach them [Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer] in good positions, they have this talent to create special things and I am very happy the three forwards have scored.

"We need to put them in the best situations. I am happy for the three of them. They played for the team."

'Sanchez will undermine everything they do'

Yet questions remain over Sanchez, who allowed King's low strike to go straight through him for Fulham 's equaliser and then tamely parried Timothy Castagne's shot into a dangerous area for Garcia to head in from close range to set up a nervy finish.

"They have strengthened in every position of the pitch but you cannot take a chance on goalkeepers," said Neville.

"I've said before it's the most difficult position on the pitch, it's the one that carries the most scrutiny and if you have got a goalkeeper who's making mistakes and is anxious, it will undermine everything you're trying to do.

"It's a problem. You've got to say it's a problem."

King's equaliser in the 23rd minute had an expected goals on target (xGoT) value of just 0.05, making it the lowest-rated shot to result in a goal during the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

In other words, Sanchez really should have saved it.

He did make a number of other saves, but he also conceded a corner after failing to clear the ball before it ran out of play and was later unconvincing when coming off his line to deal with a long ball, with Antonee Robinson missing the target to let him off the hook.

While Alonso defended his goalkeeper after the game, in his pre-match news conference on Thursday he had said: "The pitch is the boss of everything. I don't decide. The players need to show me."

That message applied to his goalkeepers - Sanchez and number two Mike Penders, 21, who is waiting to make his debut after returning from a successful loan spell at Strasbourg.

With the transfer window still open, many Chelsea fans will be asking whether the club need a new first-choice goalkeeper.

As Carragher said: "They have to sort the goalkeeping issue out because it's going to come back and haunt them again this season as it did tonight."

articles.title: Troy Deeney's Team of the Week: Trafford, Mendy, Guehi, Palmer, Pedro
articles.summary: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
articles.body:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

James Trafford ( Leeds ): It's been a big-pressure move for Trafford going to Leeds . I think at the World Cup with England he thought, 'I should be playing more' and he obviously didn't get the time and needed a move away. He produced a strong performance for Leeds at Nottingham Forest and was one of the few goalkeepers to keep a clean sheet.

Keane Lewis-Potter ( Brentford ) : He was excellent defensively and attacking wise and got his goal. He is one of Brentford 's underrated players and sort of sums up their team. Nobody speaks about him or Brentford but they hammered Tottenham .

Nobel Mendy ( Hull City ) : He was so good and powerful. He offered so much defensively to Hull and scored their second goal. He was a real powerhouse. Hull will definitely need him and he is one of those defenders where you think, 'I don't want to play against him'.

Maxence Lacroix ( Chelsea ) : Lacroix just added a level of experience and calmness to Chelsea and also got an assist. He read the game and understood what was needed and provided the maturity that will add so much to Chelsea going forward. It was a very good debut for the France defender.

Maxim de Cuyper ( Brighton ) : He scored, had an assist and was excellent for Brighton . Opponents Aston Villa were poor, but if you watched the first 20 minutes you would see he was really aggressive and really set the tone with the pressure.

Marc Guehi (Man City) : I'll have Guehi in as my holding midfielder. He should have scored two against Bournemouth because he missed a massive chance before he ended up scoring. But he got the equaliser and offered a lot more of a calming presence than City's £116m record signing Elliot Anderson - Guehi controlled the game a little bit more.

Vitaly Janelt ( Brentford ): He is one of those big, powerful and dominant players who does the basics really well. He mixed that with a goal against Spurs and you don't really speak about him, but he was always the one breaking up play and doing the horrible things really well.

Christos Tzolis ( Arsenal ) : A lot of people are talking about Arsenal and how they're great. That is absolutely true. And so is the bit of business they did bringing this young man in from Club Brugge. So many goals and assists he brings to the team, but also a calming influence and tenacity as well. Look at Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, he feels to me like both of them in one. He has a lot more output than those guys. He's going to be a beast for this year.

Anthony Elanga ( Newcastle ): Last season I though he was treated poorly by Eddie Howe because he was one that kept being put on the bench, being introduced late or would be the first one to come off. But he showed in a new formation, under a new manager and somebody who believes in him that he can use his pace and power. As a result he looks like a completely different player and he looked happy. He ran past Milos Kerkez like he wasn't there despite the Liverpool left-back having a five-yard start and produced an unbelievable finish for his goal.

Cole Palmer ( Chelsea ) : One we were all talking about, and should've gone to the World Cup with England. Feels like he's got a point to prove, feels like he's been working hard. The injuries from last year skewed everyone's vision. Everything he did at Fulham was positive. Ran forward with pace, looked like he could move. He had those issues with the groin but now he's chopping and turning.

Joao Pedro ( Chelsea ) : My old Watford team-mate and someone who will make everyone question when they said he wasn't good enough. He's going to have a breakout year.

Sergej Jakirovic ( Hull City ) : Tactically brilliant and had a gameplan for Manchester United . His side gave a bit of space away but wouldn't get transitioned on, gave away a lot of cheap fouls. Went forward in the wide areas, crossed it and finished the action. He was very impressive in the Championship last year, spoke well but never got too high or too low. He'll take a few by surprise but I'm concerned they won't have the quality in the team. For now, who cares?
